title: US embassy alerts by publication time, from Wayback captures of each embassy's alert feed
description: One row per alert an embassy or consulate published (country of the post, exact UTC time, title, type from the title). For replaying triage's embassy alert notices (kind alert; security and demonstration alerts count, weather, health, event and routine do not).

sources.name: US embassy and consulate alert category RSS feeds, as captured by the Internet Archive
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain (embassy websites, state.gov)
sources.attribution: U.S. Department of State, U.S. embassies and consulates (usembassy.gov); captures by the Internet Archive Wayback Machine

differences: Live Cordon reads the feeds directly (or a Google News search when they 403) for posts of countries at advisory level 3-4 plus a fixed list, and keeps ten per post; here every embassy in the list is read, from archived feeds.
An alert published and pushed off the ten-item feed between two captures is missing.
An edited alert keeps its first publication time here; Cordon's Google News fallback can re-date an edited alert.
Palestine has no embassy of its own: alerts of US Embassy Jerusalem (il.usembassy.gov) are rows for place IL, and copied to PS when the title or summary names the West Bank, Gaza or Palestinians.

biases: Under-counts alerts in busy periods (many alerts between captures) and for embassies with few archived captures.
Over-represents embassies whose feeds the Archive captured often, which are the large and the newsworthy ones.
Countries with no operating embassy (Iran, and Afghanistan, Syria, Yemen where their sites were not archived) have no rows, which is not the same as no alerts.

row_schema.place: ISO alpha-2 of the post's country
row_schema.source_ref: the Wayback capture of the feed that first showed the alert
row_schema.title: the alert title as posted
row_schema.summary: first 240 characters of the feed's excerpt
row_schema.first_seen: capture time that first showed it, UTC
